AI for Transport and Logistics - Route Optimisation to Customer Comms

By Craig Wilson  ·  Category: Industry Use Cases  ·  Read time: 6 min  ·  Keyword: AI for transport logistics Australia

Australian transport and logistics businesses are spending too much on fuel, too many hours on manual tracking, and too much time answering "where's my delivery?" Here are the AI systems addressing all three.

AI for Australian transport and logistics delivers measurable ROI in three areas: route optimisation (8–15% fuel cost reduction for fleet operators), customer communication automation (60–75% reduction in inbound "where is my delivery?" calls), and freight document processing (70–80% reduction in processing time). For a fleet of 20 vehicles at current Australian diesel prices, an 8–15% fuel saving alone typically covers implementation costs within 12–18 months.

Australian freight and logistics is a sector under sustained margin pressure. Fuel costs, labour costs, and the customer expectation of real-time visibility have all increased simultaneously. The businesses that will sustain margins in this environment are those that operate most efficiently. According to the Bureau of Infrastructure and Transport Research Economics (BITRE), freight volumes in Australia are projected to grow 26% by 2030 - making operational efficiency a compounding advantage for businesses that build it now.

Three AI systems delivering real value in AU logistics

Route optimisation

Most transport operators use route planning software. Most route planning software optimises for distance. Real-world route optimisation is more complex: traffic patterns by time of day, vehicle capacity utilisation, time window constraints for deliveries, driver fatigue regulations under the Heavy Vehicle National Law, and fuel cost differences between route options.

AI route optimisation systems incorporate all these variables and continuously recalculate as conditions change. A vehicle that started the day with an optimal route may need a real-time reroute by 9am if traffic, a cancelled delivery, or a breakdown changes the picture.

Realistic outcome: Fuel cost reductions of 8–15% are commonly reported for fleet operators implementing AI route optimisation. For a fleet of 20 vehicles at current Australian fuel costs, this is a meaningful annual saving - typically $30,000–$80,000 per year depending on fleet size and fuel consumption.

Delivery tracking and customer communication automation

"Where is my delivery?" is the highest-volume customer inquiry for most logistics operations - and it's entirely automatable. An AI communication system monitors vehicle GPS, delivery status updates, and exception events, and sends proactive updates to customers at defined milestones: dispatch confirmed, out for delivery, estimated arrival window, and delivery confirmed or exception notification.

Realistic outcome: 60–75% reduction in inbound "where is my delivery?" calls. Customers who receive proactive updates are measurably more satisfied than those who have to chase - even when the delivery experience is otherwise identical.

Freight document processing

Proof of delivery, consignment notes, customs documentation, dangerous goods declarations - logistics document volumes are high and the processing is largely manual. An AI document processing system captures, classifies, and extracts data from freight documents - whether PDFs, photos of paper documents, or structured electronic files - and enters data into the TMS or billing system automatically.

Realistic outcome: Document processing time reduced by 70–80%. Billing cycles shorten because documents are processed immediately rather than batched at end of day or week.

Integration with Australian TMS platforms

The effectiveness of AI logistics systems depends heavily on integration with your existing Transport Management System. Australian operators using CargoWise, Microlistics, Freight2020, or similar platforms have different integration pathways than those using generic logistics software or Excel-based operations.

What AI implementation costs for a transport and logistics business

Discovery Sprint ($5,000–$12,000): Assesses your current TMS, fleet technology, and the highest-ROI starting point. For most operators, route optimisation has the fastest payback.

Phase 2 Build - Route Optimisation ($30,000–$65,000): Integration with your existing TMS and fleet tracking, AI optimisation engine, and driver-facing interface. Typically 5–8 weeks to build.

Phase 2 Build - Document Processing + Communications ($35,000–$70,000): Both systems built together, typically for operators wanting to address both customer experience and back-office efficiency simultaneously.

Frequently asked questions

How much does AI for logistics cost in Australia?

A Discovery Sprint costs $5,000–$12,000. Route optimisation for a 15–30 vehicle fleet typically costs $30,000–$65,000 to build and integrate. Most operators see full payback within 12–18 months through fuel savings alone - the communication and document processing savings are additional.

Does AI route optimisation work with our existing fleet tracking system?

Route optimisation systems integrate with the major Australian fleet tracking platforms (Teletrac Navman, Webfleet, Verizon Connect, and others). The specific integration pathway depends on your platform, which the Discovery Sprint assesses.

How does AI route optimisation handle the Heavy Vehicle National Law requirements?

The Heavy Vehicle National Law fatigue management requirements are built into the route optimisation constraints - the system won't generate a route that requires a driver to exceed legal driving hours. This is configured as a hard constraint in the system design.
